chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban, from Mis'm ibn Abd al-Malik, said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who applies henna does not have intercourse.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, why does the one who applies henna not have intercourse?' He said: 'Because he is in a state of ihram (constricted/restricted).'

key_terms.فِدَاكَ: may I be your ransom (a term of respect)
key_terms.مُحْتَصَرٌ: constricted, restricted, or in a state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Why does the Imam prohibit sexual intercourse for one who applies henna?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits sexual intercourse for one who applies henna, defining the state as 'muhtasar' (constricted or restricted). While often linked to the ritual 'ihram' of Hajj, Shia scholars interpret this as a state of ritual preparation or temporary sanctity where the physical act of intimacy is suspended, reflecting a broader ethic of mindful transition between states of worship and daily life.
